items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 3 at 1:20AM EST until November 3 at 2:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Seas 5 to 7 feet.

* WHERE...Volusia-Brevard County Line to Jupiter Inlet 0-20 nm.

* WHEN...Until 2 PM EST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

items.headline: Flood Warning issued November 2 at 9:15PM EST until November 3 at 9:30AM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
items.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Brevard County in east central Florida...
Eastern Indian River County in east central Florida...
Northeastern Martin County in east central Florida...
St. Lucie County in east central Florida...

* WHEN...Until 930 AM EST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. It will take
several hours for all the water from the heavy rain that has
already fallen to work through local drainage systems in urban
areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 914 PM EST, Flooding is already occurring in the warned area.
Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated additional
downpours developing and moving over already saturated ground.
- This replaces the existing Flood Warning. If heavy rain persists,
additional Flash Flood Warnings may be required overnight.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Port Saint Lucie, Palm Bay, Melbourne, Walton, Fort Pierce,
Sebastian, Stuart, Vero Beach, Satellite Beach, Fellsmere, Indian
River Shores, Malabar, Indialantic, Vero Beach South, Gifford,
Winter Beach, Wabasso, Sebastian Highlands and Roseland.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
items.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
